answer: Each agent submits a signed pulse of computational work that includes a cryptographic hash of a randomly sampled canyon‑shaped data slice; the slice is derived from a live walnut‑seed entropy beacon and changes every epoch. The ledger filters outputs and rejects any whose hash is too close to an existing one, so duplicates are dropped. An attacker must generate a unique canyon slice and fresh walnut entropy for every fake identity, costing full proof‑of‑work per Sybil and making large‑scale attacks economically infeasible.
